presentation_title: Coding with AI: Generate Simple Code
learning_objectives: Use an AI tool to generate a basic Python code snippet.
outline: Have you ever struggled to start coding?
Step 4: Understand and Test the Code
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy. No prior coding knowledge is required, but a basic understanding of what code does will be helpful.

slides.title: Welcome to Coding with AI
slides.narration:
Hello.
Welcome to this **Spoken Tutorial** on Coding with **AI**.
slides.image_prompt: A friendly robot helping a person code on a laptop, simple and approachable style.

slides.title: Learning Objective
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to use an **AI** tool.
You will make it generate a simple **Python** code.
slides.image_prompt: A checklist or a target icon, representing a learning goal.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration:
You need a computer with internet.
Also, use a web browser like **Chrome** or **Firefox**.
We will use a free online **AI** tool.
slides.image_prompt: A laptop with a browser window open, showing a search bar, simple icons for internet and computer.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration:
You should know how to use a computer.
You do not need to know coding.
But it helps to know what code does.
slides.image_prompt: A stack of books or building blocks, representing foundational knowledge.

slides.title: Have you ever struggled to start coding?
slides.narration:
Have you ever wanted to write a small program?
Did you not know how to start?
Or did you search online for code for a long time?
**AI** can help us here.
slides.image_prompt: A person looking confused at a computer screen with code, with a question mark above their head.

slides.title: Introducing Google Bard
slides.narration:
Today, we will use **Google Bard**.
It will help us make code.
**Bard** is a free **AI** tool.
It understands your requests and gives output, like code.
slides.image_prompt: Google Bard logo or a stylized representation of an AI chatbot interface.

slides.title: Step 1: Open Google Bard
slides.narration:
Let us see an example.
First, open your web browser.
Go to **bard.google.com**.
You may need to log in with your **Google** account.
slides.image_prompt: A browser window showing `bard.google.com` homepage, with a login prompt.

slides.title: Step 2: Write a Clear Prompt
slides.narration:
Now, tell **Bard** what code you want.
A clear request gives better output.
In the chat box, type: Write a **Python** function to add two numbers.
slides.image_prompt: A screenshot of Bard's chat interface with the prompt `Write a Python function to add two numbers.` typed into the input box.

slides.title: Step 3: Get the Generated Code
slides.narration:
Type your **prompt** and press Enter.
**Bard** will show you the **Python** code.
It also gives a small explanation of the code.
slides.image_prompt: A screenshot of Bard's interface showing the generated Python code for adding two numbers, along with a short explanation.

slides.title: Step 4: Understand and Test the Code
slides.narration:
**Bard** has given us the code.
It is important to understand it.
The code makes a function named **add_numbers(a, b)**.
This function adds the values of **a** and **b**.
Copy this code.
slides.image_prompt: A code editor showing the copied Python code, with a small play button icon.

slides.title: Step 5: Run the Code
slides.narration:
You can paste this code into a **Python** editor.
For this tutorial, we will see the output **Bard** gave.
The example **print(add_numbers(5, 3))** shows the output will be 8.
slides.image_prompt: A simple console output showing `8`, next to the Python code.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, we used **Google Bard**.
We learned to make it generate simple **Python** code.
We saw how to open **Bard**, write a clear **prompt**, and understand the code.
slides.image_prompt: A whiteboard with key points summarized, a person pointing to it.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Your assignment is to use **Google Bard**.
Ask it to make a **Python** function that multiplies two numbers.
Also, ask it to show an example of how to use this function.
slides.image_prompt: A person working on a laptop, with a thought bubble showing Python code for multiplication.
